post.description:
Ingest chute pod logs streamed by the in-guest log shipper.

mTLS-only, via the cvm proxy: the guest presents its per-boot registry mTLS leaf and the
``resolve_log_context`` dependency binds the shipment to the launch-config owner (cross-miner
injection is rejected there; the auth result is cached per (config_id, cert) so a burst of
batches doesn't re-verify). Identity is derived server-side — the body carries only
``deployment_id`` + the log lines.

Cutoff contract (docs/specs/chute-log-shipper.md): **204** = stop capturing this pod,
**200** = keep sending, **403/404** = terminal reject (unauthorized / unknown config), which
the guest also treats as stop. The lines are ingested BEFORE the cutoff is evaluated so a
final crash batch is always stored.

In the Depot proxy flow this endpoint is called by nginx auth_request to
verify the miner before nginx proxies to Depot's token endpoint; it only
needs to return 200 on success (or 401 on failure).

The VM's attested measurement version decides which auth is required:

- version >= registry_mtls_min_version: mTLS.  The nginx frontend forwards the
  client cert as X-Client-Cert; the leaf is verified against the CA registered
  for the VM.  No legacy fallback — a VM this new must use mTLS.
- otherwise (older VM, or unknown IP): legacy Bittensor hotkey/signature/nonce.

Setting registry_mtls_min_version to "0.0.0" forces every attested VM onto
mTLS — the kill switch that closes the legacy "any registered miner can pull
any private chute" hole once the fleet is fully migrated.

The require_registry_proxy_secret dependency, when REGISTRY_PROXY_SECRET is configured,
rejects requests that do not carry X-Registry-Proxy-Auth matching the secret,
preventing X-Client-Cert / X-Real-IP spoofing on connections that bypass the
registry proxy.  The mTLS client cert is extracted (typed) by extract_optional_client_cert.

This endpoint is called by VMs during boot before any registration.

without it. When supplied it is bound into the nonce, and boot attestation enforces that

that omit it get an unbound nonce and the binding check is skipped.

post.description:
Verify boot attestation and return LUKS passphrase.

Both VM generations reach this route, so the hotkey proof is EXTRACTED rather than required:
a presented signature is verified here and 401s if it does not hold, but its absence is left
for the handler to judge once the quote names the attested image. See
process_boot_attestation, which requires a proof from any image whose measured initramfs
ships the signer.

Verifies the TDX quote against the expected boot measurements and returns the LUKS passphrase
for disk decryption if valid. For VMs >= 1.3.0 it also returns a luks_quote_nonce for the
following runtime call (POST /provision on 1.4.0+, POST /luks/attest on 1.3.x); for 1.4.0+ it
additionally returns root_next + root_confirm_nonce and the VM's ephemeral auth SS58.

Rotate LUKS passphrases for new-format VMs (version >= 1.3.0).

DEPRECATED: superseded by POST /provision, which does the same storage rotation and
additionally records the VM root CA identity. Kept unchanged for legacy in-field VMs;
retire once the fleet upgrades.

The VM embeds the luks_quote_nonce (received in the boot attestation response)
in a TDX quote after extending RTMR3 in initramfs. require_luks_quote_nonce
validates and consumes the nonce; the handler then calls verify_quote which
checks the TDX signature and all RTMR measurements including RTMR3. Returns
rotated passphrases, the k3s encryption key, and a confirm nonce.

Confirm or discard pending LUKS passphrase rotation results.

DEPRECATED for the storage-rotation flow: new VMs use POST /provision/confirm (same
shared logic). Kept for legacy in-field VMs; note the boot-phase root-passphrase confirm
still uses this route until /luks/* is fully retired.

The VM reports per-volume success/failure. require_confirm_nonce validates
and consumes the nonce before the handler runs. Volumes with rotated=True
have pending passphrases promoted to current; rotated=False discards pending.

Provision a new VM at runtime: record its root CA identity and issue storage secrets.

Only 1.4.0+ VMs reach this route (it is behind require_cvm_proxy), and every one of them
signs, so require_hotkey_auth demands a proven hotkey at the door -- no backwards-compatible
"unsigned is acceptable" case exists here, unlike boot attestation. The proven identity is
what the rc gate in verify_quote is given.

The RTMR3-attested runtime entry point for new VMs (supersedes /luks/attest going
forward). The VM presents its per-boot root CA as the mTLS client cert; the quote's
REPORTDATA binds SHA256(that cert's pubkey), so the same cert_hash check that guards
/luks/attest also proves CA possession — no bespoke quote logic is needed.
require_luks_quote_nonce validates and consumes the runtime nonce; the handler verifies
the quote (signature + all RTMR measurements incl. RTMR3), records
server.vm_root_ca_cert (idempotent), and returns rotated passphrases, the k3s encryption
key, and a confirm nonce.

Confirm or discard pending storage-passphrase rotations from POST /provision.

Delegates to the same shared logic as the legacy /luks/confirm (process_luks_confirm):
require_confirm_nonce validates and consumes the nonce, then volumes with rotated=True
have pending passphrases promoted to current and rotated=False discards pending.

The accepted AMD SEV-SNP measurements: the launch digest a report's MEASUREMENT must equal,
per published VM image and host class. The report must also meet its product line's
requirements (GET /servers/snp/product_lines).

Release candidates are never listed. No authentication required — public transparency endpoint.

What an AMD SEV-SNP report must satisfy beyond its measurement, per AMD product line: the ARK
fingerprint its VCEK chain must end in, the CPU variants accepted (by the report's CPUID family,
model and stepping) with each one's minimum reported TCB, and the PLATFORM_INFO and
mitigation-vector bits that must be set.

Everything a third party needs to repeat our acceptance checks. A product line or variant not
listed is not accepted. No authentication required — public transparency endpoint.

Return host profiles: the platform inputs a measurement is built from.

By default, only host classes that HAVE measurements. Each entry's `tee_type` says which
platform it attests under. Find `fingerprint` in the `fingerprints` of that platform's
measurements (GET /servers/tdx/measurements or /servers/snp/measurements), regenerate the
measurement from the
inputs here, and compare -- that makes every published measurement independently
reproducible, and a quote holder can see which host class their own measurement corresponds
to. A third party needs no flags and can never be handed an unverified claim.

`include_pending=true` also returns host classes awaiting generation. That is the measurement
generator's queue: a profile becomes measured only once measurements are generated for it, and
generation has to fetch it first. Each entry's `measured` flag says which set it is in.

Public and unauthenticated, so the generation side needs no database credentials. Every entry
is host-class data: the machine-identifying fields are dropped at submission and never stored,
and the submitter's `miner_hotkey` is a column this query never selects.

post.description:
Register a host class (sek8s `discover-profile.sh` output) so Chutes can measure it.

One of four distinct operations: this REGISTERS, POST /servers/tdx/host_profiles/status
RESOLVES a class (is it known, and for which images), POST /servers/tdx/preflight CHECKS whether
one specific image can boot, and GET /servers/tdx/host_profiles LISTS the generated set. A miner
reaches this only when the status lookup reports the class is not on file. The API owns the
fingerprint -- the miner sends raw platform metadata and gets back the class's retention
lifecycle, which only ever advances:

  * `accepted` -- a measurement has already been generated for this class; retained from here on
  * `pending`  -- parked in object storage, awaiting its first measurement generation

A real submission is always stored, so this never returns `unknown`. It answers only whether the
class has been measured at all; whether the caller's specific image can boot is preflight's job.
Signed by the miner hotkey, so the signature covers the request body.

Is this Intel TDX host class known, and which VM images cover it? The check
`chutes-cvm host verify` runs, and the launch's Step 1. An AMD class is answered by
POST /servers/snp/host_profiles/status.

Deliberately version-free: a miner verifies a host BEFORE downloading any image, so this asks
only about the topology -- "can this host run anything at all, and if so what".

  * `measurements` non-empty -> the class is attestable; those are the images it can launch.
  * empty, `status: pending`  -> registered, awaiting measurement generation. Nothing to do but
    retry later; re-submitting will not speed it up.
  * empty, `status: unknown`  -> never submitted. Register it with
    POST /servers/tdx/host_profiles.

A POST because the API owns the fingerprint: a caller cannot ask about "my topology" without
handing over the profile to be fingerprinted. Stores nothing -- the read-only counterpart to the
submission route. Signed by the miner hotkey, so the signature covers the request body.

Is this AMD SEV-SNP host class known, and which VM images cover it? The same question as
POST /servers/tdx/host_profiles/status, for SEV-SNP classes.

Each covered image also carries `acpi_sha256`: the hash of the class's ACPI tables, which
the guest firmware checks against `sek8s.acpi_sha256` on the kernel cmdline. The launch puts it
there; without it the image cannot boot.

Can this exact image boot on this host? The one call a launch/upgrade preflight makes.

A check against both a host profile and the measurement set, so it hangs off neither. The API
fingerprints the submitted profile and answers whether a published measurement for the caller's
`(version, rc)` carries that fingerprint -- the whole launch decision in one boolean:

  * `launchable: true`  -> the VM will attest; launch.
  * `launchable: false` -> register the class (POST /servers/tdx/host_profiles), then retry once
    Chutes publishes its measurement.

Stores nothing and reveals nothing beyond the answer -- not the full measurement set, not
whether a profile row exists. Signed by the miner hotkey, so the signature covers the body.

get.description:
Return the signed key bundle used by booting VMs to fetch and verify cosign/Helm keys.

Each entry in 'keys' is a base64-encoded public key; the corresponding entry in
'signatures' is a base64-encoded RSA signature (PKCS#1 v1.5 over SHA-256) produced
offline by the root signing key in Cloud KMS. Nothing here can sign; this only serves.
Intentionally public — no mTLS required. Independent third parties and auditors can
fetch these public keys to verify TDX quotes without needing to be a VM client.

false) so miners can still see which servers remain out of date against the last target.

HostProfile.description:
One host class, as chutes-cvm's ``HostProfile.to_api_profile()`` submits it.

A direct translation of the client's own model: the RTMR0 determinants and nothing else.
Stored == hashed == required, one set. An unhashed field stored beside a hashed one would
re-split the class at the byte level -- two hosts that measure identically would differ in the
stored row, and first-write-wins would silently drop one of them. That is why host RAM, BDFs,
DMI strings and the lspci tree are absent rather than merely excluded.

Every block forbids extras, so a client that adds a key 422s until the API models it: add the
field here, deploy, then roll out the client.

HostProfileCpu.title: HostProfileCpu
HostProfileCpu.description:
The host CPU facts that reach RTMR0: the guest -smp and the SMBIOS Type-4 identity.

Mirrors chutes-cvm's `HostCpu` field for field. `processor_id` is nullable -- CPUID leaf-1 is
unreadable on some hosts -- but the key is required, and generation refuses a null rather than
measuring its own host's CPU.

HostProfileGpuDevice.title: HostProfileGpuDevice
HostProfileGpuDevice.description:
One passthrough GPU.

Unlike the other endpoints, a GPU must report BARs. They are what the measurement generator
reproduces as a `pci-bar-stub`, so a GPU with none yields a guest whose MMIO windows -- and
therefore RTMR0 -- do not match any real boot. That is not a host we can measure, and storing
it would create a class whose published measurement nothing can attest against.

HostProfileIbDevice.title: HostProfileIbDevice
HostProfileIbDevice.description:
One InfiniBand device, plus the two flags that decide whether it is passed through.

`is_bridge_pf` comes from VPD, which needs root -- an unprivileged capture reports every PF
as non-bridge.

HostProfileMeasurement.title: HostProfileMeasurement
HostProfileMeasurement.description:
One published VM image that covers a host class: its version and rc flag. All an Intel TDX
class needs: its ACPI is attested through RTMR0.

HostProfileMemory.title: HostProfileMemory
HostProfileMemory.description:
Guest RAM, as the client resolved it.

Not host RAM: the sizing rules are per-GPU-profile and live in chutes-cvm, so the client sends
the answer. Storing the host total instead would split hosts that measure identically -- 2007
and 2011 GB are one H200 class.

HostProfileNuma.title: HostProfileNuma
HostProfileNuma.description: Host NUMA node count: it picks the guest's memory-map and PXB-PCIe grouping.

HostProfileNvswitchDevice.title: HostProfileNvswitchDevice
HostProfileNvswitchDevice.description: One NVSwitch. Its BARs shape the guest DSDT, so it is modeled like any other endpoint.

HostProfilePciBar.title: HostProfilePciBar
HostProfilePciBar.description:
One MMIO window of a passthrough device, from an lspci "Region N" line.

Offline measurement generation reproduces these windows with a ``pci-bar-stub``, so the
guest ACPI it measures matches what a real passthrough launch produces -- which makes the
layout an RTMR0 input, and part of the class fingerprint. Most BARs are fixed per GPU model,
but the large one (BAR2 on H200/B200/RTX) is RESIZABLE: host firmware sets its current size,
so two otherwise identical machines can need different RTMR0s. Fingerprinting the layout is
what keeps those apart instead of collapsing them into one class whose measurement only one
of them can attest against.

HostProfileQemu.title: HostProfileQemu
HostProfileQemu.description: The QEMU that builds the guest ACPI measured into RTMR0.

HostProfileResponse.title: HostProfileResponse
HostProfileResponse.description: Public entry for GET /servers/tdx/host_profiles: one generated host class.

HostProfileStatus.title: HostProfileStatus
HostProfileStatus.description:
Retention lifecycle of a submitted host class -- monotonic, only ever advances
(unknown -> pending -> accepted) and never regresses.

``accepted`` is class-level and version-agnostic: a measurement was generated for this
fingerprint at some point, so the class is on the attestable set and retained (its profile is
kept for RTMR0 regeneration). It is NOT the answer to "can version X launch here" -- that is
POST /servers/tdx/preflight, which joins the caller's (version, rc) to the class's measurements.
Submission only reports which of the three the class is in; POST
/servers/tdx/host_profiles/status reports the same lifecycle without storing anything.

HostProfileStatusResponse.title: HostProfileStatusResponse
HostProfileStatusResponse.description:
Response for POST /servers/tdx/host_profiles/status: is this host class known, and for
which images? POST /servers/snp/host_profiles/status answers with ``SnpHostProfileStatusResponse``.

The read-only counterpart to the submission response, and the gate `chutes-cvm host verify`
runs. Deliberately version-free -- a host is verified before it has downloaded any image, so
nothing here depends on what the caller happens to have on disk. Whether one SPECIFIC image can
boot is POST /servers/tdx/preflight.

LogLine.title: LogLine
LogLine.description: One CRI log line as shipped by the guest.

deployment_id.title: Deployment Id
deployment_id.description: From the chutes/deployment-id pod label; empty if absent. Never used for auth.

LogShipmentArgs.title: LogShipmentArgs
LogShipmentArgs.description:
Request body for POST /instances/launch_config/{config_id}/logs.

``deployment_id`` is the sole top-level metadata field: it is non-security
correlation data (Grafana filtering only) that the validator cannot derive
from ``config_id`` in the pre-registration window, so the guest supplies it
from the ``chutes/deployment-id`` pod label. It is never used for auth.

PreflightResponse.title: PreflightResponse
PreflightResponse.description:
Response for POST /servers/tdx/preflight: can this exact image boot on this host?

A check against both a host profile and the measurement set, so it hangs off neither -- it
fingerprints the submitted profile and asks whether a measurement for the requested image
covers it.

PreflightResult.title: PreflightResult
PreflightResult.description: Result of a maintenance preflight eligibility check.

quote.title: Quote
quote.description: Base64-encoded TDX quote (runtime type, RTMR3 extended)

volumes.title: Volumes
volumes.description: Volume names to rotate passphrases for

ProvisionRequest.title: ProvisionRequest
ProvisionRequest.description:
Request model for POST /servers/{vm_name}/provision.

The runtime (RTMR3-attested) provisioning entry point for new VMs. The VM presents its
root CA as the mTLS client cert; the quote's REPORTDATA binds SHA256(that cert's pubkey),
so the CA identity is recorded from this call. Mirrors the luks/attest body today (quote
+ volumes) and is the extensible home for future provisioning inputs.

ProvisionResponse.title: ProvisionResponse
ProvisionResponse.description:
Response model for POST /servers/{vm_name}/provision.

Carries the storage-provisioning secrets today (rotated volume passphrases, k3s
encryption key, confirm nonce); shaped to extend with future provisioning outputs.

host.title: Host
host.description: Public IP address or DNS Name of the server

name.title: Name
name.description: Server name (defaults to server id if omitted)

ServerMaintenanceStatus.title: ServerMaintenanceStatus
ServerMaintenanceStatus.description:
TEE server maintenance phase (servers.maintenance_status). Once requested, a server stays in
pending/maintenance until it boots at the upgrade target version.

ServerUpgradeStatus.title: ServerUpgradeStatus
ServerUpgradeStatus.description: A TEE server and its version relative to the upgrade target.

SnpCpuVariant.title: SnpCpuVariant
SnpCpuVariant.description:
One CPU variant of an AMD product line: the report CPUID fields that identify it, and the
minimum reported TCB accepted from it.

SnpHostProfileMeasurement.title: SnpHostProfileMeasurement
SnpHostProfileMeasurement.description:
An SEV-SNP class's covered image: also the ACPI hash the guest firmware checks, which the
launch puts on the kernel cmdline (sek8s.acpi_sha256).

SnpHostProfileStatusResponse.title: SnpHostProfileStatusResponse
SnpHostProfileStatusResponse.description: Response for POST /servers/snp/host_profiles/status: each image also carries its ACPI hash.

SnpMeasurementResponse.title: SnpMeasurementResponse
SnpMeasurementResponse.description: An accepted AMD SEV-SNP measurement: the launch digest a report's MEASUREMENT must equal.

SnpProductLineResponse.title: SnpProductLineResponse
SnpProductLineResponse.description:
What an SEV-SNP report from one AMD product line must satisfy, beyond its measurement:
everything a third party needs to repeat our acceptance checks.

SnpTcbVersion.title: SnpTcbVersion
SnpTcbVersion.description:
The four SVNs of an SEV-SNP TCB_VERSION: what a report or VCEK carries, and the
minimum we accept per CPU variant (``snp.product_lines`` in the TEE config).

Unpacks the Milan/Genoa layout (see docs/amd-sev-snp.md); Turin's differs. AMD's
security bulletins state minimum TCBs in these terms (e.g. "TCB[SNP] >= 0x1B").

SoleSurvivorBlock.title: SoleSurvivorBlock
SoleSurvivorBlock.description: An instance that is the sole active instance for its chute.

TdxMeasurementResponse.title: TdxMeasurementResponse
TdxMeasurementResponse.description:
An accepted Intel TDX measurement: the registers a runtime quote must carry. A boot quote
carries the same values except RTMR3, which is all-zeros until runtime.

evidence.description: TEE evidence for each instance of the chute

failed_instance_ids.title: Failed Instance Ids
failed_instance_ids.description: Instance IDs for which evidence could not be retrieved (instances still exist but evidence fetch failed)

excluded_instance_ids.title: Excluded Instance Ids
excluded_instance_ids.description: AMD SEV-SNP instances left out because the request did not include them (include_amd). They exist and serve the chute; pass include_amd=true to get their evidence.

TeeChuteEvidence.title: TeeChuteEvidence
TeeChuteEvidence.description: TEE evidence for a chute: list of evidence per instance (from instance evidence endpoints).

tee_type.description: Platform that produced `quote`: `tdx` (Intel TDX) or `snp` (AMD SEV-SNP)

quote.title: Quote
quote.description: Base64-encoded TDX quote, or SEV-SNP attestation report when tee_type is snp

gpu_evidence.title: Gpu Evidence
gpu_evidence.description: Per-GPU evidence: list of dicts (each GPU's evidence/certificate already structured; evidence fields are base64 where applicable)

instance_id.title: Instance Id
instance_id.description: Instance ID (present when part of a chute's evidence list)

certificate.title: Certificate
certificate.description: Base64-encoded DER format TLS certificate from the server

signature.title: Signature
signature.description: Base64-encoded RSA-PKCS1v15-SHA256 signature of attested_body, signed with the host TLS private key. Present on attestation proxy >= 0.2.0. Verifying this against the certificate public key proves the responder holds the attested private key.

attested_body.title: Attested Body
attested_body.description: Base64-encoded raw response body from the attestation proxy—the exact bytes covered by signature. Present when signature is present.

TeeInstanceEvidence.title: TeeInstanceEvidence
TeeInstanceEvidence.description:
TEE evidence for a single instance: the platform quote, GPU evidence (per-GPU dicts), and
server certificate.

TeeMeasurementResponse.title: TeeMeasurementResponse
TeeMeasurementResponse.description:
Public response model for a single accepted TDX measurement (legacy shape).

Predates AMD support, so it is TDX-only and keeps the boot/runtime RTMR dicts existing
clients parse. Both are built here from the entry's registers; the boot set differs only
in RTMR3, which is all-zeros until the guest stack is measured at runtime.

TeeType.title: TeeType
TeeType.description: Confidential-computing platform that produced a piece of attestation evidence.

UpgradeWindowInfo.title: UpgradeWindowInfo
UpgradeWindowInfo.description: Summary of an upgrade window for API responses.
